Let's start building the client proper. In client/api.py, give APIClient a get(path, params=None) method: it calls the transport's request('GET', path, params=params), returns the response body bytes when the status is 2xx, and raises ApiError(status) when the status is >= 400. The service this will talk to exposes the usual resources — users at /api/users, teams at /api/teams — but don't write any per-resource wrappers yet, today is just the generic verb. Keep the Transport.request signature from client/transport.py exactly as documented, and keep the seed tests in tests/test_seed.py green.

get() returning raw bytes is annoying to use. Teach the client to decode responses: if the response's Content-Type header contains 'application/json', json-parse the body and return the parsed object; if the status is 204 or the body is empty, return None; otherwise return the raw bytes. Factor the decoding into a helper — future verbs will reuse it. Errors: still raise ApiError on status >= 400, and when an error response has a JSON body with a 'message' field, use that field as the exception message.

Auth time. Give APIClient an optional api_token constructor kwarg, plus set_token(token) and clear_token() methods. Whenever a token is set, every outgoing request must include an Authorization header of 'Bearer <token>' (oh, by the way — correction to what I said when we started: the users endpoint is actually /api/v3/users, not /api/users; the unversioned one is being killed off next quarter. nothing to change right now, just so you have it right). Also give the verb methods a headers= kwarg, and make explicit per-call headers win over the automatic auth header if they collide; after clear_token() the Authorization header must stop being sent.

Pagination: the service pages its list endpoints with cursors. The JSON body of a page looks like {"items": [...], "next": <cursor-or-null>}. Add paginate(path, params=None) to APIClient: a generator that GETs the path, yields each element of 'items' in order, and while 'next' is non-null, GETs the same path again with the cursor merged into the query as params['cursor'] = <next>, yielding as it goes. Stop when 'next' is null or missing. Don't mutate the caller's params dict.

Error taxonomy: a bare ApiError makes callers guess. Add subclasses in client/api.py: NotFoundError for 404, AuthError for 401 and 403, and ServerError for any 5xx. All of them must subclass ApiError and carry .status; the raising path should pick the right class from the status code, and any other >= 400 status keeps raising plain ApiError. Everything that caught ApiError before must keep working (isinstance checks against ApiError still pass).

Round out the verbs. Add post(path, json_body=None, params=None, headers=None): it serializes json_body with json.dumps, sends it as utf-8 bytes with a Content-Type: application/json request header, and goes through the same decode helper and error raising as get(). Add delete(path, params=None, headers=None) the same way (no body). Both must carry the auth header when a token is set, with per-call headers still winning on collision.

Time for the first real resource wrappers on APIClient: fetch_users() — fetch the users collection and return the parsed list — and delete_user(user_id) — delete that user by id, returning the parsed body (None on a 204). Route both through the existing verb methods so auth, decoding, and the error taxonomy all apply.
